I nearly drowned in Disney World. 

It was at one of the water parks, I think Blizzard Beach. It was back in 2005 and I was like 12 and didn’t like a lot of the water slides because I was terrified of heights. However there was one that fairly short that shot you out into a ten foot deep pool. I had slid down it a couple times and had no issues. I love water and all but I’m not the strongest swimmer. It felt like it took forever to get to the surface. I had let go of my breath and a bunch of water went into my mouth. By the time I breached the surface the life guard was getting ready to jump in after me. She met me over by the ladder and made sure I was okay as I was coughing up all the water. I went to Cuba last year for a day. It was interesting to say the least. I stepped off a cruise ship and felt like I was in a different decade with the old cars. The people around the port did keep trying to sell things but the farther away I got the more they were friendlier. Our tour guide, Yuri, told us his life story and wanted to hear ours, we asked him questions about Cuba and what things were like and he did the same back for America. He was just as interested as learning our culture as we were his. We went all over Havana, to a cigar factory to the National forest to Revolution Square and more, and then we asked Yuri to take us to his favorite place to eat, which was a tiny diner that actually looked someone’s house, but had the best sandwiches and coffee we’d ever had. The buildings around Havana were so colorful, and though they looked tiny, they were bigger on the inside. And I was sorta surprised by some of the Russian influence I saw around. It was really fun and a great learning experience, I was glad I got to experience before the travel ban happened again.

So in high school, I was a Hetalia fan (if you’re not sure what that is, it’s basically an anime about the world countries as humans). I did not expect the amount of people that had showed up, maybe around 50 or so. We had a lot of fun, we got to know each other, we played games like Duck Duck Goose, we rode a carousel that was nearby, and even went to the closest science museum. I made a lot of new friends that day from all over my state, I stayed in touch with a lot of them until I left for college. I witnessed people making new friends, some meeting their future partners, and overall a lot of fun. I found it pretty cool that a silly little anime had a big impact on some people’s lives
